newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan OKs record '96 foreign equity fund entry.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan OKs record '96 foreign equity fund entry.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday that foreign funds permitted to enter the island's stock market reached a record US$27.1 billion in 1996 -- nearly triple the 1995 level.
Far less than that amount has actually entered Taiwan, but officials say the soaring levels of applications for permits, which are mandatory, indicate growing interest in local stocks.
The commission attributed the huge jump in approvals mainly to Morgan Stanley Capital International's incorporation of its Taiwan stock index into its global emerging market index in September.
"Many foreign funds have increased their investment ratio in our market since the Morgan Stanley move," a commission official told Reuters.

From January 1 to December 30, the commission approved 268 applications for foreign fund entries worth $27.1 billion, a 171 percent increase in value from 1995, when it approved 105 applications worth $9.99 billion, the official said.
In December alone, the commission approved 27 applications worth $1.84 billion against 13 applications worth $1 billion in December 1995, he said.
The watchdog commission does not keep updated figures for how much money actually enters Taiwan under its permits.

Cumulative totals show that US$13.5 billion has entered since Taiwan's market was opened to foreigners in 1992 and that US$4.7 billion has been repatriated, indicating that some US$8.8 billion remains in Taiwan, the commission official said.
Foreign fund approvals should rise in 1997 as the government further liberalises the financial markets, he said.

In November, the central bank eased restrictions on foreign ownership of local stocks, raising the maximum level allowed to 25 percent of total market equity from 20 percent. The cap had been raised from 15 percent in March.
In mid-December, the commission said it had raised the investment ceiling for individual foreign funds in the local market to $600 million from $400 million.
Foreign funds can apply for additional entries above the individual ceiling on a case-by-case basis, it said.
